newsitem.title: USA: Hawaii says downgrade will not hurt market access.
newsitem.headline: Hawaii says downgrade will not hurt market access.

text.p: Hawaii Gov. Ben Cayetano said on Saturday the state should continue to have "favorable access" to the capital markets despite a ratings downgrade by Standard & Poor's Corp.

"The credit ratings will allow the state continued favorable access to the capital markets," the governor said in a statement, adding that the state expects to issue about $590 million of general obligation bonds next week.

On Friday, Standard & Poor's Corp said it cut Hawaii's general obligation bond rating to A-plus from AA, affecting $2.5 billion of debt. The rating was taken off CreditWatch, where it was placed on December 11, 1996.
S&P said the downgrade reflected the state's rising debt levels, with substantial additional debt likely for the next bienniumn, and deteriorating financial performance.
Cayetano said S&P's concern is partly understandable.
"In light of the most recent projections by the Council on Revenues and recent arbitration awards and settlements, S&P's concern about financial performance is understandable," the governor said.

"On the other hand, concern about rising debt levels caused by a substantially increased construction program appears to be misplaced because while total debt outstanding will increase, debt service as a percentage of revenues will decline," the governor said.
By increasing construction spending, the state will create over 3,000 jobs, stimulate personal income growth and boost the lagging construction sector, Cayetano said.
